title: Client-server and peer-to-peer
starter: A class of 30 needs to share one big video file. Describe two ways it could be done, and say which would be quicker.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Client-server model
facts: A central server provides services such as files, logins, email or web pages.
Clients request services from the server, and the server responds.
Used by most schools and businesses.
stations.challenge: Name three services your school's servers provide when you use a computer.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A central server provides services such as files, logins, email or web pages.
Also credit: Clients request services from the server, and the server responds.

questions.q: In a client-server network, what does a client do?
questions.a: Requests services, such as files or web pages, from a server

questions.q: Which of these is acting as a server?
questions.a: A computer that stores students' files and checks their logins

stations.name: Peer-to-peer model
facts: There is no central server: every computer is an equal peer.
Peers share files and resources directly with each other.
Each user looks after their own files, security and backups.
stations.challenge: Where might you find a peer-to-peer network at home?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: There is no central server: every computer is an equal peer.
Also credit: Peers share files and resources directly with each other.

questions.q: What is a peer in a peer-to-peer network?
questions.a: A computer that both requests and provides resources, as an equal

questions.q: Who is responsible for backups in a peer-to-peer network?
questions.a: Each user, for their own computer

stations.name: Client-server: pros and cons
facts: Easier to manage security, backups and software updates from one place.
Expensive to set up, and needs IT specialists to maintain it.
The server is a single point of failure.
stations.challenge: Why does a school choose client-server rather than peer-to-peer?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Easier to manage security, backups and software updates from one place.
Also credit: Expensive to set up, and needs IT specialists to maintain it.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of a client-server network?
questions.a: It is easier to take backups of all the shared data

questions.q: Why is the server a single point of failure?
questions.a: If it stops working, the clients can't reach the files and services it provides

stations.name: Peer-to-peer: pros and cons
facts: Cheaper and easier to set up: no expensive server is needed.
No dependency on a single machine.
Less secure, harder to keep files organised, and users must do their own backups.
stations.challenge: A family business has three computers. Would you recommend peer-to-peer? Why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Cheaper and easier to set up: no expensive server is needed.
Also credit: No dependency on a single machine.

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of peer-to-peer?
questions.a: Users need to manage their own backups

questions.q: Why is peer-to-peer usually cheaper to set up?
questions.a: No expensive server hardware is needed

stations.name: Who's who?
stations.challenge: Label each device on the wall diagram as a server, client or peer.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Servers provide services and resources.

questions.q: Match each role to what it does.
questions.a: Server → Provides services and resources to other computers; Client → Requests services from a server; Peer → Both requests and provides resources, as an equal

questions.q: A games console downloads an update from the manufacturer's server. What is the console?

stations.name: How torrents work
facts: A big file is split into many small pieces.
Your computer downloads different pieces from lots of other users at once, and uploads pieces to others.
The more people sharing, the faster it can be.
stations.challenge: Is torrenting client-server or peer-to-peer? Is it a quicker or slower way to download big files, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A big file is split into many small pieces.
Also credit: Your computer downloads different pieces from lots of other users at once, and uploads pieces to others.

questions.q: Torrenting is an example of which model?
Why can torrent downloads be fast?
questions.a: Pieces come from many peers at the same time, so no single server limits the speed

final.name: Final challenge: client-server or P2P?

questions.q: Does each statement describe client-server or peer-to-peer?
questions.a: Each user has to back up their own machine = Peer-to-peer; Files end up scattered and hard to find = Peer-to-peer; No expensive central machine to buy = Peer-to-peer; One nightly backup covers everyone's shared work = Client-server; Carries on working if one computer is switched off = Peer-to-peer; Security settings are hard to apply consistently = Peer-to-peer; Permissions are set once, centrally = Client-server; Needs trained staff to look after it = Client-server; New software can be pushed to every machine at once = Client-server; Costs more to buy and to run = Client-server; Anyone can set it up without training = Peer-to-peer; Everything stops if the central machine fails = Client-server

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: Describe what a server does in a client-server network.
points: A central server provides services such as files, logins, email or web pages.
Clients request services from the server, and the server responds.
The server is a single point of failure.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: Give two reasons a small office might choose peer-to-peer.
points: A big file is split into many small pieces.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: A school is choosing between client-server and peer-to-peer. Recommend one and justify your choice using two characteristics.
points: A central server provides services such as files, logins, email or web pages.
Clients request services from the server, and the server responds.
Used by most schools and businesses.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 6.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
